title: Minimax ATE Estimation When Treatment and Outcome Labels Are Rarely Observed Jointly
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The finite-intensity result is a certified variational and computational characterization, not an explicit least-favorable-margin phase map

the uniform likelihood expansion with estimated margins, random stratum retention, and masses approaching the retention threshold is asserted without quantitative score, Hessian, boundary, and remainder bounds sufficient to establish the displayed uniform L1 remainder

Even treating that gap as repairable, fixed finite d, the specific MCAR annotation design, outcome nondegeneracy, and the absence of a numerical implementation or phase-map example constrain the leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a marked-Poisson split-label experiment, finite decision programs, a global certificate, and uniform transfer across rare strata. The math and panel reviews passed, but D0.5 rated the delivered package subfield below the field floor. The Gaussian attainment proof needs quantitative uniform bounds, and the explicit phase map and numerical implementation remain open.
tldr: Separate treatment-only and outcome-only records learn the margins of a binary causal table but not the within-stratum treatment--outcome association. The effective association sample size is \(\kappa_N=Nq_N\). The minimax absolute-error and uniformly honest expected-length frontiers are characterized when \(\kappa_N\) vanishes, converges to a positive constant, or diverges. At finite intensity, projected finite \(\rho\)-nets of the unconditional-margin polytope and explicit fibre, mark-coupling, endpoint-enlargement, and coverage-repair moduli globally bracket both outer frontiers by finite linear programs, uniformly over arbitrarily rare strata and collapsing fibres. At growing intensity the limit is Gaussian with the sharp worst-case variance. The exact least-favorable finite-intensity margin phase map remains open.
gap: Existing causal annotation theory starts from a diverging number of joint treatment--outcome labels, while statistical matching describes the ambiguity when none are observed. The decision boundary at a finite expected joint count, including optimal honest intervals and unknown-margin transfer, is not characterized.
fill: The project derives the marked-Poisson and Gaussian association experiments, certifies their minimax risk and interval-length values, constructs attaining procedures, and proves the exact consistency threshold without imposing a common lower bound on stratum masses.
